newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Sabesp makes Bovespa debut.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Sabesp makes Bovespa debut.

text.p: Sao Paulo state sewage company Sabesp made its debut on the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa) Wednesday with the offer of four percent of the company's total capital, officials said.

Sabesp common stock, which opened at 278 reais per 1,000 shares, were at 285 reais in late morning trade. Forty-five trades were seen with the shares, totalling 2.735 million reais. The firm has only voting shares.
The company's decision to list its stock on the Sao Paulo bolsa is part of its strategy to increase the firm's profile among investors.
Sabesp stock had been trading on the Rio de Janeiro's SOMA over-the-counter market since November and became one of the SOMA's main blue-chips.

The company's president Ariovaldo Carmignani told reporters the state plans to gradually offer more shares to the public. The remaining 96 percent of Sabesp's capital belong to Sao Paulo state government and Companhia Paulista de Ativos (CPA), a holding covering the assets the state plans to privatize.
Sao Paulo state governor Mario Covas confirmed that there is no limit for the share offer, but he noted the state does not plan to privatize Sabesp.
"We don't have a limit, we can offer more shares later on. But we are not thinking in the direction of privatization," he said.

Sabesp officials said the company is studying the idea of selling shares to a strategic partner to add value to the firm. Carmignani said the company could follow the example of Minas Gerais state power utility Cemig which last week sold a 32.9 percent voting stake to a group led by U.S. power operators.
An eventual sale to a strategic partner, however, would take place only next year, he said.
Carmignani also announced a 9.8 percent increase in water and sewage rates as of June. The last rate adjustment took place in June last year.

Sabesp, formally known as Companhia de Saneamento Basico do Estado de Sao Paulo, operates concessions granted by Sao Paulo's municipalities and provides water and sewage services for 22 million customers in over 350 municipalities.
This year, Sabesp expects to provide services to about 20 more municipalities.

The company aims to supply 100 percent of Sao Paulo's population with treated and piped water, serving 85 percent with sewage collection and having 60 percent of this sewage treated by the end of 1998.
In 1996, Sabesp invested 748 million reais, nearly doubling from the 384 million reais invested in the previous year. In 1997, the company plans to spend 1.1 billion reais.

Since 1995, Sabesp has been posting profits following a deep restructuring process. The company posted a 134 million reais net profit in the first quarter. Last year, it reported a 373.6 million reais net profit, adjusted for inflation, the best performance of its history.
Sabesp sees revenues reaching three billion reais this year, up from 2.45 billion reais in 1996.
